title: Function→ToolLink compatibility proxy and name-scoping rules
creator: Priya Kumar
description:
Problem: Many customers use our legacy 'functions' call surface while new integrations and partner ecosystems expect an OpenAI-style 'tool' contract. Incompatible naming, streaming semantics, and metadata shapes cause failures during rollouts and make migration painful.

Goal: Implement a lightweight compatibility proxy and a set of deterministic name-scoping rules so that legacy function invocations can be routed to tool implementations (and vice-versa) with preserved provenance, correct streaming boundaries, and predictable fallbacks. This should enable safe progressive rollouts and reduce customer friction while we converge on a single canonical call surface.

Scope: runtime proxy layer (non-breaking), name-scoping policy, alias registry, migration CLI to backfill historical call mappings, integration tests for streaming + function/tool combined flows, and a small console UI to inspect ambiguous aliases (follow-up UX epics will expand this).

Non-goals: full deprecation of legacy functions (separate program), UI/console heavy UX redesigns (only an inspection view now), and automated telemetry-based renames without customer opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime proxy routes legacy function calls to tool implementations when a definitive mapping exists and returns identical token stream markers to callers.
Ambiguous names are rejected with clear 409 error and a suggested alias list (no silent remapping).
Streaming across a mapped call boundary preserves chunk order and function-call start/finish signals (tests assert token offsets).
Integration suite exercises 10K synthetic calls including name collisions; <0.5% false-positive remaps and zero dropped streams.
Migration CLI can produce a dry-run mapping report and apply mappings to alias registry; tested against 100k rows of call logs in staging.
All changes covered by unit and e2e tests with CI gating and a perf benchmark showing <3% p95 latency regression for the proxy hop under synthetic load.

comments: 2026-02-20 Priya Kumar: Created ticket after spike. Spike notes attached in Confluence link; spike showed several edge cases around streaming start/stop tokens when tool invocation is proxied.

2026-02-24 Rafael Ortiz: Design draft uploaded. Primary decision: deterministic scoping rule takes precedence over probabilistic aliasing — we will only use probabilistic suggestions in console, not for runtime remap. Leaving open whether to support cross-namespace overrides (discuss next week).

2026-02-27 Emma Chen: Reviewed runtime approach; suggested to add a lightweight provenance header (x-rw-call-orig) to preserve original surface name and version for audit logs — will add to runtime headers. Added tests for provenance header propagation.

2026-03-01 Jonah Blake: QA noted a streaming regression in initial canary: reordering of final function-close marker when proxy applied with batching. Reproduced with minimal harness and added failing test. Rafael assigned to fix by 2026-03-05.

2026-03-02 Rafael Ortiz: Patch pushed to PR #8572 to enforce flush-before-call behavior so function-close markers are emitted before proxy hands off to tool. Benchmarks show 1.8% p95 latency increase but resolves ordering failures. Requesting reviews from Emma and Jonah.
tradeoffs: Proxy adds a hop which increases p95 latency; mitigated by in-process resolver and connection pooling.
Strict deterministic mapping prevents silent remaps and customer surprise but requires more manual alias management. We'll provide tooling to ease operational burden.
Probabilistic alias suggestions are useful for console-assisted migration but are intentionally NOT used for runtime remapping to avoid correctness issues.
migration_plan: 1) Create alias registry with initial mappings from spike/dry-run report (opt-in).
2) Run proxy in passive mode (logging + no remap) for 48h to evaluate collisions and false positives.
3) Apply mappings to canary namespace for a small set of customers with rollback enabled.
4) Expand rollout across regions, run backfill to tag historical call logs with resolved tool IDs.
5) After N weeks and no major incidents, consider defaulting mapping for free-tier customers; enterprise customers will be notified before any automatic remap.
